title: Re-baseline Tier 3's timeout and/or decouple seeding from benchmark execution
summary: Even after CIF-4 speeds up seeding, 500k-row seed + full matrix + 200-VU/15-min Locust ramp + IR metrics may still not comfortably fit in 120 minutes on a shared runner — measure post-fix and either raise the timeout, cache a pre-seeded corpus, or split seeding into its own job.
description:
Depends on CIF-4 landing first. The Tier 3 job (`.github/workflows/benchmark-suite.yml`, `timeout-minutes: 120`) currently does, in one job: seed 500k rows, run the full `benchmark_pr` matrix at 500k rows, run a 200-VU/15-minute Locust ramp, then deterministic IR metrics at scale. CIF-4 fixes the seed step's throughput, but the *sum* of all four phases still needs to be re-measured against the 120-minute budget before assuming the job is healthy — a 15-minute Locust ramp alone plus a full matrix at 500k rows is not free.

Once CIF-4 lands, measure a real end-to-end Tier 3 run (or as much of it as can be run locally/in a scratch workflow dispatch) and then choose among:

1. **Raise `timeout-minutes`** if the post-fix total is close to but over 120 minutes and there's no cheaper structural fix — simplest option if the numbers support it.
2. **Cache/reuse a pre-seeded corpus** across runs instead of reseeding 500k rows from scratch every single Tier 3 run — e.g. a Db2 container volume snapshot or a pre-built data dump restored at container start, invalidated only when the corpus generator (`seed_corpus.py`'s content/metadata generation logic or `--seed`) changes. This turns an O(500k inserts) step into an O(1) restore on every run after the first.
3. **Split seeding into its own job** (or a separate workflow_dispatch step with its own artifact/checkpoint persisted between jobs), so a slow or failing seed doesn't also consume the time budget the benchmark/Locust/IR steps need, and so partial seeding progress survives a downstream failure instead of being redone from row 0 on every retry (note `seed_corpus.py` already supports checkpointing — lines ~247-299 — so this may be more about workflow structure than script logic).

Acceptance: a full Tier 3 `workflow_dispatch` run (suite=`tier3-scale`) completes without hitting the job timeout, and the consolidated report shows real numbers for the full benchmark matrix, Locust ramp, and IR metrics at 500k-row scale — the first time this has happened for this job.
